content.text:
I've finished and submitted: my pick is **index 13 (Ni 0.58, Sb 0.42)**, which had the highest EQE I measured, **0.236%**.

I used all 3 merit measurements:

| Index | Ni : Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.34 : 0.66 (the NiSb₂O₆ composition) | 0.0048 |
| 13 | 0.58 : 0.42 | **0.236** |
| 7 | 0.75 : 0.25 | 0.068 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE seems to be highest in the middle of the composition line, near a 1:1 Ni:Sb ratio. It falls off sharply on the Sb-rich side and less steeply on the Ni-rich side.
- **Why I chose these three:** I started with index 21 because it matches a known compound (NiSb₂O₆), but it came out almost zero. I then tested one point in the middle and one on the Ni-rich side.
- **Main uncertainty:** with only three points, the real best composition could be a nearby one I didn't measure (roughly indices 10–17). My score depends only on what I measured, so any gain there is lost.
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. They couldn't have added merit measurements, so I don't know which crystal phases are actually present in these films.
